title: Symmetry Properties of Circles: Chords and Tangents
seo_title: Sec 3 Symmetry properties of circles Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: symmetry properties of circles: equal chords are equidistant from the centre; the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre; tangents from an external point are equal in length; the line joining an external point to the centre bisects the angle between the tangents
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on symmetry properties of circles: perpendicular bisectors of chords, equal chords, tangents from an external point and tangent-radius right angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord; a tangent meets the radius at 90°.
key_sub: Tangents from an external point are equal. Use Pythagoras' theorem with the radius.
body_html:
How it works

  • The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, and the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre.
  • Equal chords are equidistant from the centre (and chords equidistant from the centre are equal).
  • A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
  • Tangents from an external point are equal, and the line from the point to the centre bisects the angle between them.
  • Each fact gives a right angle, so use Pythagoras' theorem with the radius as the hypotenuse.
Example

A chord is 16 cm long and the radius is 10 cm. How far is the chord from the centre?

Half the chord = 8 cm

√(10² − 8²) = √36

Answer: 6 cm

Example

Tangents TA and TB meet at T with ∠ATB = 50°. Find ∠AOB.

∠OAT = ∠OBT = 90°

360° − 90° − 90° − 50°

Answer: 130°

Common mistakes

  • Using the whole chord instead of half of it in Pythagoras' theorem.
  • Adding squares when the radius is the hypotenuse and you need a shorter side.
  • Forgetting to double the half-chord at the end.
  • Thinking ∠AOB equals ∠ATB. They add up to 180°.

faq.q: What are the symmetry properties of circles?
faq.a: The perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord, equal chords are equidistant from the centre, tangents from an external point are equal, and the line from that point to the centre bisects the angle between the tangents.

faq.q: Why is a tangent perpendicular to the radius?
faq.a: The radius to the point of contact is the shortest distance from the centre to the tangent line, so it meets the tangent at 90°.

faq.q: How do I find the length of a chord?
faq.a: Draw the perpendicular from the centre. Use Pythagoras' theorem with the radius as the hypotenuse to find half the chord, then double it.

faq.q: What is the angle between two tangents and the angle at the centre?
faq.a: They add up to 180°, because the two right angles at the points of contact make 180° of the 360° in the kite.
